summary: The bad() path takes data = Byte.MIN_VALUE (-128) and computes (byte)(data * 2). The int product -256 is out of the byte range, so the narrowing cast to byte silently wraps (integer underflow), producing 0. The fix keeps the multiply-and-print feature but stores the product in an int, which can represent -256 exactly and never underflows. Legitimate values still multiply and print correctly; nothing is disabled or made constant.
